overview_text: History, culture, and law is an interdisciplinary major that offers students an opportunity to understand how legal systems are shaped by cultural norms and historical developments, as well as how social change has been and can be created through legal processes. After studying principles of historical method and jurisprudence, students bring to bear the interdisciplinary frameworks they have begun to develop through program electives. HCL emphasizes the study of local, regional, national, and transnational histories and cultures, as well as the comparative study of law and legal history. The program requires students to develop research skills through seminars in research methodology. The broad-based education provided by the HCL major grounds students in knowledge of the historical exchange between peoples, cultures, and societies that is key to understanding contemporary issues such as international law, the future of democracy, the nature of citizenship and rights, the origins and conduct of war, the foundations of racial and ethnic conflict and tolerance, and poverty and prosperity. At the same time, the HCL major teaches crucial skills in analytical thinking, research processes, writing, oral expression, and multimedia presentation. This program is currently only available to former Marymount Manhattan College students who are eligible for continued enrollment at Northeastern University. This program includes required courses that will be taught on ground at the Northeastern New York City campus.
